newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA WINS AUSTRIAN-OMINATED WORLD CUP SLALOM.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA WINS AUSTRIAN-OMINATED WORLD CUP SLALOM.

text.p: Thomas Sykora won the season's first World Cup slalom for men Sunday in a race that vividly demonstrated Austria's slalom dominance.

Racing in bright sunshine, Sykora prevailed with a time of 1:46.03, just ahead of teammate Thomas Stangassinger, clocked in 1:46.32. Kjetil Andre Aamodt of Norway broke the Austrian monopoly, taking third in 1:46.91, but another Austrian, Christian Mayer, took fourth in 1:47.08.
Norwegian veteran Ole Christian Furuseth was fifth and Michael Tritscher of Austria sixth. The Austrians held the top four positions, in the same order, after the first run.
Kiminobu Kimura of Japan was a surprisingly strong seventh-place finisher, one of the best in the alpine World Cup history of that nation.
In claiming his third career victory, the 28-year-old Sykora skied almost perfectly on the first run, then held himself strongly under control for the victory.

Aamodt, again showing good form in trying to regain the overall title he won in 1994, made a strong challenge on the second run, shaving six-tenths of a second off Sykora's advantage. Kimura, only 15th after the first run, had the fastest time on the second.
